name: MongoDB C Driver
reason: No numeric comparison against any baseline found. The GitHub page (opened) makes no performance claims; the sibling repo mongodb/mongo-c-driver-performance (opened) only implements the cross-driver DriverBench microbenchmarks and its README lists no results, baselines or comparisons. A WebSearch for published C or C++ driver throughput versus other MongoDB drivers found only benchmark infrastructure (the DriverBench spec itself says cross-language numbers are not directly comparable) and no results.

name: MongoDB C++ Driver
reason: No numbers against any baseline. README and benchmark/README.md (opened) describe a DriverBench microbenchmark suite (BSONBench, SingleBench, ParallelBench, ReadBench, WriteBench, RunCommandBench) with no results; the only comparison language is that an inMemory mongod should be used when comparing against other drivers. Repo issue search for benchmark/performance/faster/slower shows no comparative figures. A WebSearch found no published mongocxx vs other-driver throughput (one forum thread reports 7k ops/sec for id queries as a complaint, not a comparison).

name: MySQL++
listed_description: A C++ wrapper for MySQL's C API.
reason: No numeric baseline comparison reachable. The project site (tangentsoft.net) is blocked from this session (WebFetch getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so its docs could not be read. WebSearch for MySQL++ performance versus the MySQL C API or SQLite returned nothing about MySQL++; the closest hit was the Boost.MySQL benchmark page, which compares Boost.MySQL (not MySQL++) with libmysqlclient and other-language drivers. A wrapper over the C API is not expected to beat it, and no claim was found.

name: nanodbc
listed_description: A small C++ wrapper for the native C ODBC API.
reason: No numeric baseline comparison found. README (opened, raw copy saved and grepped for bench/perf/fast/speed/slow: no matches) only compares usability with the verbose C ODBC API; the GitHub issue list for benchmark/performance terms shows no comparison, and issue #241 (insertion speed with the PostgreSQL driver) reports only the author's own before and after rates (about 2k rows/s vs up to 100k inserts/s with a multi-row VALUES string) with no other library or raw ODBC baseline. A WebSearch for nanodbc vs raw ODBC or other libraries found no benchmark. The project docs site (nanodbc.github.io) is on the blocked *.github.io class and was not fetched.
